correctness.rationale: Every non-spine vertex has degree two, so each page is forced to have one of the listed types relative to the two spine colours. When spine colours agree, complete pages are independently grouped and at least floor(b/2) share the spine colour. When spines differ, the exhaustive four page types are constrained exactly by p+x>=floor(b/2)+1 and p+y>=floor(b/2)+1. Factorials choose page types and Stirling numbers count unlabelled remaining colour classes without overcounting. Both cases are necessary and sufficient. Maximizing number of non-spine colour classes forces exactly the two stated extremal types; Pascal identity gives binomial count. The standalone direct graph-based set-partition exhaustive verifier tests b=1..4 (120333 partitions overall) and formula checks b=5..20, with VERIFY_OK. Finite checks are corroboration only; proof works for every b>=1.
